units.translation: a silent destruction.
to perish
I perish.

Thus from the apograph for ποινὰς ὀλέκῃ [with penalties you destroy]. ὁλέκω [I destroy] and ὀλέκομαι [I perish] is an epic verb, which the tragedians rarely used. Another example is Sophocles Tr. 1013 ὠλεκόμαν ὁ τάλας [I was perishing, wretched me]. - See Thes. vol. 6 p. 1869.
For what sin are you perishing by way of penalties?

There is one example of the imperfect
The aorist ὤλεσα [I destroyed] is very frequent.
In the sense of losing
Thus Wellauer for ἀπώλεσε δήτα [he destroyed indeed].
Perfect
Thus Porson for τἀπολωλόθ᾽ — ἐγώ [the things that have been destroyed — I].
Middle form
Thus Turnebus for ἑλοίμαν [I might take], which in M is made from ἑλοίμην [I might take for myself].
where, as the sense demands, I restored ὀροίμαν [I might be roused].

Corruptly at line 842 σοῦσθε σοῦσθ᾽ ὀλόμεναι ὀλόμεν᾽ ἐπαμίδα [hasten, hasten, perishing, perishing, upon the reaper], where Hermann corrected to ὀλοαὶ μέγ᾽ ἐπ᾽ ἄμαλα [destructive greatly upon the sheaves]. Of the participle ὁλόμενος [perishing] the epic form οὐλόμενος [accursed, destructive] means deadly, pernicious; there is one example
and in Euripides Phoen. 1527 (which he calls ὀλοὰς τύχας [destructive fortunes] at 554).
